scope: Open-weight models a consumer machine runs: 32 GB of VRAM and 128 GB of RAM (160 GB summed) hold the weights at Q4_K_M or higher precision and an 8-bit KV cache of at least 64K tokens (owner, 2026-11-18). Q4_K_M is a floor: a model that fits only at a lower quantization (Q3, IQ3, Q2) does not count, and a run seen at one is evidence only once scaled up to Q4_K_M. What must fit is the resident memory: gb_64k less ssd_tables_gb, the lookup tables (Engram tables, for example) that its card or inference framework documents as kept on SSD and read on demand, at the same precision, cited in ssd_tables_source; without such a source everything counts. A local model is ranked as a reviewer only among these, by its base model's place on a board (model_signals.may_review); the ids are the base models as the boards name them, and aliases their other spellings on the boards (lowercase, spaces as hyphens).
formula: gb = weights + KV, in 10^9 bytes. Weights: total_b x 4.85 bits / 8 (Q4_K_M's average), total_b the Hub's parameter count (a vision tower included). KV at 8 bits: 2 (K and V) x attention layers (full_layers; a sliding-window layer counted as a full one, an upper bound) x KV heads x head_dim x tokens (65,536 and 131,072), from the card's config.json; linear-attention (Gated DeltaNet) and Mamba layers keep a fixed state, not counted.

Seen at IQ3_XXS only, below the Q4 floor, so not proof by itself: it runs with a 128K int8 KV cache in the RTX 3090's 24 GB plus about 43 GB of host RAM for its experts (relay/native_deployments/swift-next.json: local-labs swift-next card, Strata b742ff9, Swift-1.5 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS, 128K int8 KV; the host RAM from node/tare_node/config/qualified_model_fleet.json). At Q4_K_M it needs at most (24 + 43) x 4.85 / 3.06 = 106.2 GB, KV included (scaling the KV too only overstates it). No public parameter count.
